title: Boss: the numbers do not add up
summary: A torn metrics snapshot, a config loaded twice, and an inventory that oversells: each fixed and proven under every interleaving.

steps.title: The ticket
body: 12:00:10 metrics total=10977 ok=10859 failed=118     # off by 0 this time
09:14:02 config loaded (pricing.json, 1.2 MB)        # twice, 3 ms apart
17:41:55 reserved sku=GPU-4090 qty=3 left=2          # two customers, 5 in stock, both got 3
Each of these is a race. Each fix is checked by running the code under **every interleaving** of two threads; a wrong fix shows the

steps.title: 1. A snapshot that adds up
prompt: `Metrics.Record(bool ok)` counts every request in `Total` and in either `Ok` or `Failed`. Each counter is incremented with
`Interlocked`, so no update is lost, but a `Snapshot()` taken in the middle of a `Record` sees `Total` already increased and `Ok`
Fix **`Metrics`** so that every snapshot satisfies `Total == Ok + Failed`. Keep
`void Record(bool ok)` and `(int Total, int Ok, int Failed) Snapshot()`.
**Checked:** T1 records a success while T2 takes a snapshot, under every interleaving. The result shows whether the snapshot added
up, then the final total: it must be `True 1`.

hints: Three counters that must agree are one invariant: protect all three with one lock, in `Record` and in `Snapshot`.
steps.explain: `Interlocked` makes each counter right on its own. Relationships *between* values need one critical section, or one immutable object swapped as a whole.

steps.title: 2. Load the config once
prompt: `ConfigHolder.Get()` loads the configuration on first use. Two requests arriving together both see `_config == null` and both load
Fix **`ConfigHolder`** (constructor `ConfigHolder(Func<string> load)`, method **`string Get()`**) so that `load` runs **exactly once**,
however the first calls interleave, and every call returns the loaded value.
**Checked:** two threads call `Get()` under every interleaving; the result is `loads value1 value2` and must be `1 cfg cfg`.

interleavings.title: Two first calls at once
setup: var holder = new ConfigHolder(() => { loads++; return "cfg"; });
interleavings.resultLabel: loads, then what each caller got

hints: `Lazy<T>` exists for exactly this. Its default mode runs the factory once, even when the first calls race.
`private readonly Lazy<string> _config = new(load);` and `public string Get() => _config.Value;`. A double-checked `lock` also works.
explain: Hand-written double-checked locking (`if (x == null) lock (...) if (x == null) x = ...`) is correct in .NET only with care about
publication; `Lazy<T>` gets it right for you and says what you mean.

steps.title: 3. Never oversell
prompt: Write **`Inventory`** with a constructor `Inventory(Dictionary<string, int> stock)`, **`bool TryReserve(string sku, int qty)`**
(reserve only if enough is left; return whether it did) and **`int Left(string sku)`**.
Keep the stock in a `System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary<string, int>`, and make `TryReserve` atomic **without a
**Checked:** two customers reserve 3 of a sku with 5 left, under every interleaving. The result is `left successes`: `2 1`.
starter: public bool TryReserve(string sku, int qty)
if (!_stock.TryGetValue(sku, out var have) || have < qty) return false;
public int Left(string sku) => _stock.TryGetValue(sku, out var n) ? n : 0;
solution: public bool TryReserve(string sku, int qty)
if (!_stock.TryGetValue(sku, out var have) || have < qty) return false;
if (_stock.TryUpdate(sku, have - qty, have)) return true;
public int Left(string sku) => _stock.TryGetValue(sku, out var n) ? n : 0;

interleavings.title: Two customers, 5 in stock, 3 each
setup: var inventory = new Inventory(new Dictionary<string, int> { ["GPU-4090"] = 5 });
interleavings.resultLabel: stock left and number of successful reservations

hints: Read the current count, check it, then `TryUpdate(sku, have - qty, have)`: it only writes if the count is still `have`.
Put it in `while (true)`: if `TryUpdate` returns false someone else changed the count, so read again and re-check.
explain: In a real shop the stock lives in a database, and the same idea is a conditional update:
`UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - @n WHERE sku = @sku AND qty >= @n` and check the row count, or an optimistic concurrency token
(EF Core `[ConcurrencyCheck]` / rowversion). Same race, same cure: make the check and the write one atomic step.
